title: Donald Knuth
name: Donald Knuth
summary: Computer scientist and Stanford professor emeritus whose work on algorithms, programming languages, and The Art of Computer Programming helped establish computer science as a rigorous discipline.
whyThisMatters: Knuth's analysis of algorithms and attention to exactness shaped how programmers reason about correctness, complexity, and implementation—core concerns whenever security-sensitive code must behave predictably.

sections.overview:
Donald E. Knuth is a computer scientist and Stanford professor emeritus known for his multivolume series The Art of Computer Programming, as well as work on algorithms, programming languages, TeX, and literate programming.

Precision in computing

Security depends on programs doing exactly what their designers intend. Knuth's work on the analysis of algorithms and careful program construction helped make rigor in computer science a practical and teachable discipline.

A continuing reference

ACM awarded Knuth the 1974 Turing Award for major contributions to analysis of algorithms and programming-language design. His books and archival work remain important reference points for computing history.

timeline.event: Born in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, United States.
Completes a PhD in mathematics at the California Institute of Technology.
Publishes the first volume of The Art of Computer Programming.
Receives the ACM A.M. Turing Award.
Introduces TeX to support high-quality digital typesetting.
